checks_by_claim.source_location: Convex-body definition PDF p.9; surface-area description and Steiner formula p.10
checks_by_claim.verification: The definition expressly permits empty interior. For K=[-1,1]x{0} in R2, the parallel area is 4r+pi r^2, so Steiner's coefficient gives V1(K)=2. Its ambient boundary is K itself, so half its H1 measure is 1. This admitted example contradicts the unqualified half-boundary-area description.
checks_by_claim.counterevidence: The correctly normalised intrinsic-volume coefficient and the principal Gaussian/Wills identity remain valid, giving segment regret log(1+2/sqrt(2pi)).
checks_by_claim.impact: A local boundary-range statement is false; no principal identity is disproved.
checks_by_claim.repair: Require full dimension for half-boundary-area; use affine-span volume for codimension one.

checks_by_claim.source_location: PDF pp.19–20, beta>0 introduction and derivative conclusion after (4.3)
checks_by_claim.verification: Use the surjective constant contraction {-a,a}->{0}, a>0, retaining the two source indices as in the proof. At beta=1/2 and s=a^2(1-t), the Gaussian coordinates are plus/minus sqrt(s)Z and the exact expectation is F_(1/2)(t,t)=2+2exp(-s/2), strictly increasing. All Gaussian moments exist and repeated target coordinates are allowed. Re-deriving Hessian and variance drift gives (beta-1)/4 times sum E[f p_i p_j](Delta_ii+Delta_jj-2Delta_ij). The bracket is nonpositive; the asserted decrease therefore needs beta>=1.
checks_by_claim.impact: The intermediate parameter range is too broad. The main comparison only requires beta tending to infinity, so it survives the checked beta>1 argument.
checks_by_claim.repair: Choose beta>1. The exponential soft-max sandwich and Gaussian integrability justify the limit; finite-subset lifting gives the stated extension without an infinite-dimensional Lebesgue density.

checks_by_claim.source_location: Lemma 4.1 PDF p.20 and actual interpolation p.19
checks_by_claim.verification: The lemma misprints covariance matrices in place of Gaussian vectors. The correct definition is X(t)=sqrt(1-t)X^A+sqrt(t)X^B, already used by the main comparison proof. A literal scalar reading is inconsistent, but no actual invalid derivation is shown to use it. The corrected report retains F3 and its notation correction without counting a substantive Minor.

The Gaussian envelope integral follows by comparing any predictive density to the envelope and normalising when finite. Tonelli plus Steiner's polynomial yields the Wills coefficients with their (2pi)^(-j/2) normalisation, including a segment and singleton. These support the report's stated positive scope; they do not certify the separate full redundancy lower bound or generic chaining results.
